1. Heard Shri Rakesh Tripathi-I, learned counsel for the petitioner, Sri Himanshu Shukla, Advocate,
holding brief of Sri Bhupendra Kumar Tripathi, learned counsel for the respondent No.4 and learned Standing Counsel appearing for the State-respondents.

2. This writ petition is preferred for the following principal relief:

sentences.text:
"(a) issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus commanding the respondents No.3, Executive Officer, Third Nirman Khand, Public Work Department (PWD), District Ghazipur not to construct the road over petitioner's Araji No.201,
area about 0.8320 hectare situated at Village- Chakahlad Badaura, Post Para,
Pargana and Tehsil- Mohammadabad, District- Ghazipur, without adopting procedure prescribed under Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

(b) issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus commanding the respondent No.2 to decide the representation of the petitioner dated 02.09.2023,
after providing opportunity of hearing to the petitioner."
3. Petitioner claims to be owner of the Araji No.201, area about 0.8320 hectare situated at Village- Chakahlad Badaura, Post Para, Pargana and Tehsil- Mohammadabad, District- Ghazipur.
He is aggrieved that the respondents are carrying out construction of road without according compensation to the petitioner.

He fairly states that he has no objection, in case the land is utilized for the development purposes, specially laying or widening the road but at the same time,
respondents may ensure the adequate compensation to the petitioner in the light of Government Order dated 12th May, 2016, issued by State Government.
He further submits that he has already moved a detailed representation dated 2.9.2023, which is pending consideration before the District Magistrate, Ghazipur.
4. Learned Standing Counsel very fairly submits that, in case, any such representation/application is pending, the same would be decided by the concerned authority.
5. Considering the facts and circumstances, we are not inclined to keep the matter pending consideration.

6. Without expressing any opinion on the merits of the issue and with the consent of counsel for the parties, the writ petition stands disposed of asking the District Magistrate, Ghazipur to look into,
examine and redress the grievance of the petitioner strictly in accordance with law expeditiously,
preferably, within six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order, but certainly after giving opportunity to all the stakeholders in the matter.
Suffice to indicate that the Court has not adverted into the merits of the case.
